traits.notes: Multiple images show the same seedling with 7-8 leaves arranged in a whorl at the apex of a short, green, woody stem. Leaves are simple, elliptic, with entire margins and pinnate venation. Some leaves show minor damage such as holes and light discoloration, but no clear signs of herbivory or pathogens are inferred. The stem has white patches and lenticels. No stipules, latex, or pulvinus are visible. The overall structure suggests a young seedling with a rosette of leaves.

=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at a single node, visible in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the apex of the stem, forming a rosette-like arrangement)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade, not divided into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations, visible in all images)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends, consistent across leaves)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point, visible in multiple images)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broad and curved, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex with lateral veins branching off, visible in close-ups)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced moderately, 5-7 pairs per leaf (clearly visible in images 1, 4, and 5)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface reflects light, appears glossy in multiple images)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, not exceeding 1-2 cm, visible in images 3 and 5)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, no wings or grooves, visible in images 3 and 5)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem is thick, green, and appears firm with some lenticels, visible in images 3 and 4)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green with white patches (stem is primarily green, with some white or pale areas, possibly lenticels or exudate, visible in images 3 and 4)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): lenticellate (small, raised, pale spots consistent with lenticels visible on stem surface)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf base in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no milky sap visible when stem is broken or damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base, and leaf complexity is simple, not compound)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible)

F. Notes: Multiple images show the same seedling with 7-8 leaves arranged in a whorl at the apex of a short, green, woody stem. Leaves are simple, elliptic, with entire margins and pinnate venation. Some leaves show minor damage such as holes and light discoloration, but no clear signs of herbivory or pathogens are inferred. The stem has white patches and lenticels. No stipules, latex, or pulvinus are visible. The overall structure suggests a young seedling with a rosette of leaves.
